name: Big Pine Campground
note: Lassen NF (Hat Creek RD) drive-in campground, ~19 sites under tall pines along Hat Creek, 1 mi south of Old Station on SR 44/89; max 2 vehicles/site, FCFS (fee on arrival), open ~Apr-Oct. --Claude

name: Crater Lake Campground
note: Lassen NF (Eagle Lake RD) drive-in campground, 17 sites on Crater Lake (no gas motors; fly-fishing/canoeing), 7 mi off Hwy 44; fire rings/tables, hand-pump water, vault toilets, FCFS, open ~Jun-Oct. Access road is rough and steep - large motorhomes/trailers are discouraged, but a compact 23-ft rig can manage. RV Life 0*(unrated)/$ (auto 7/2026). --Claude

name: Hat Creek Campground
note: Lassen NF (Hat Creek RD) developed campground along Hat Creek, ~72 sites incl. reservable individual + group units, flush toilets, potable water; 1.5 mi south of the Hwy 44/89 jct at Old Station; partly reservable on recreation.gov, open ~Apr-Oct. --Claude

name: Cave Campground
note: Lassen NF (Hat Creek RD) developed campground right on Hat Creek, ~46 drive-in sites with fire rings/BBQs, flush toilets, potable water; 1/4 mi north of the Hwy 44/89 jct at Old Station; FCFS, open ~Apr-Oct (North Loop temporarily closed). --Claude

name: Bridge Campground
note: Lassen NF (Hat Creek RD) drive-in campground, ~24 sites along Hat Creek ~4 mi north of Old Station on Hwy 89; vault toilets, no potable water, low-fee FCFS (max 2 vehicles/site), open ~Apr-Oct. RV Life 0*(unrated)/$ (auto 7/2026). --Claude

name: Cottonwood Flat Campground
note: Remote handful-of-sites (~5) FCFS Forest Service campground on the Devil's Garden plateau near Canby (Modoc NF), adjacent to a meadow; primitive - no restrooms or potable water. Reached by Devil's Garden gravel roads (drive-in). Open ~May-Oct, free, 14-day limit. --Claude

name: Howard's Gulch Campground
note: 11-site FCFS Forest Service campground set in a tree-lined gulch just off Highway 139, Devil's Garden Ranger District (Modoc NF) near Canby; vault toilets and a short hiking trail, drinking-water system under repair (bring water). Drive-in with paved-highway access. $15/night, open mid-May to late Oct. --Claude

name: Big Sage Campground
note: FCFS Forest Service campground on Big Sage Reservoir near Alturas (Modoc NF), surrounded by juniper and sagebrush; ~11 sites, vault toilet, picnic tables, no potable water, dirt boat launch. Free, open mid-May to late Oct. --Claude

name: Janes Reservoir Campground
note: Primitive FCFS Forest Service campground circling the southeast shore of Janes Reservoir on the Devil's Garden plateau (Modoc NF) near Alturas; ~8 sites, 2 vault toilets, picnic tables, no potable water, dirt boat ramp. Reached via ~29 mi of Crowder Flat Rd (gravel/dirt, drive-in). Free, open ~mid-May to late Oct. --Claude

name: Cherry Valley Campground
note: Stanislaus NF (Groveland RD) campground near Cherry Lake in the Hetch Hetchy watershed; 46 sites (41 single, 5 double), vault toilets, no hookups, first-come first-served (cash/check). Lake ~1.5 mi via trail; boat ramp near the dam. Motorhomes to 24 ft OK - reach via Cottonwood Rd from Tuolumne (Cherry Lake Rd is narrow/steep, not advised for RVs). Open May-Sept. --Claude

name: Hull Creek Campground
note: Stanislaus NF (Sugar Pine RD) 23-site campground in mixed conifer along Hull Creek, popular OHV staging area; vault toilets, no hookups, bring water, first-come first-served (cash). Reached via dirt FR 3N01, ~12 mi SE of Long Barn. Open May-Dec. --Claude

name: Fraser Flat Campground
note: Stanislaus NF (Sugar Pine RD) 38-site campground on the South Fork Stanislaus River, operated by the Dodge Ridge concession; vault toilets, ADA fishing piers, no hookups, first-come first-served (cash). Access via narrow Fraser Flat Rd, 3 mi N of Hwy 108 at Spring Gap; RV dump station on Hwy 108 near Pinecrest Lake Rd. Open Apr-Oct. --Claude

name: Beardsley Dam Campground
note: Stanislaus NF (Sugar Pine RD) Forest Service-operated campground near the south end of Beardsley Reservoir; 16 sites (single/double), vault toilets, potable water, no hookups, max RV/trailer 36 ft, paved road across the dam. Open Apr-Oct. --Claude

name: Caples Lake Campground
note: Eldorado NF (Amador Ranger District) campground on the south shore of Caples Lake off Hwy 88 at ~7,800 ft. 34 sites: 8 walk-in single + 1 walk-in double tent, 9 tent, and 7 tent/trailer/RV drive-in sites; no hookups, vault toilets; open ~late June-Sept. Paved state-highway access. Lake recreation facilities co-managed with El Dorado Irrigation District; campground on Forest Service land. --Claude

name: Jones Fork Campground
note: Eldorado NF FCFS drive-in campground on the Jones Fork arm of Union Valley Reservoir (off Ice House Rd); ~10 sites, tight loop, RVs to ~35 ft (a 28-ft toy hauler fit per review), open ~Jun-Sep. First-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Big Meadows Campground
note: Eldorado NF (Georgetown RD) FCFS drive-in campground near Hell Hole Reservoir, ~22 mi E of Georgetown via Wentworth Springs Rd; RVs to 40 ft, no hookups, open ~May-Nov, ~$10. First-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Buck Meadow Campground
note: Sierra NF fee campground on Deer Creek at the confluence with Snow Corral Creek, ~6,760 ft, off McKinley Grove Rd (paved and dirt). Drive-in, max vehicle length 35 ft; vault toilets, no potable water; open May-Oct. Not on recreation.gov - first-come, first-served fee site. --Claude

name: Trapper Springs Campground
note: PG&E-operated campground near the west shore of Courtright Reservoir (within Sierra NF), ~8,200 ft, off McKinley Grove/Courtright Rd. 70 drive-in sites described by the Forest Service as 'relatively flat and good for large RVs' (max vehicle length 35 ft) but without lake views; open May-Sept, $24/night. Reservable through PG&E recreation. PG&E project-reservoir land, utility-run -> ownership private per convention. --Claude  Reservations need at least 2 nights; first-come, first-served sites can be taken for one night (PG&E, 2026-10-10). --Claude

name: Hartley Springs Campground
note: Forested Inyo NF campground off US-395 / June Lake Junction near Obsidian Dome; ~20 drive-in sites among red fir and Jeffrey pine, vault toilets, no hookups, no potable water. First-come, first-served, open summer only. Sites are on the small forested side but satellite and reviews show mid-size RVs fitting the gravel spurs. --Claude

name: North Eagle Lake Campground
note: BLM Eagle Lake Field Office developed campground near the northeast side of Eagle Lake; 20 sites taking RVs/trailers up to 35 ft, no hookups, potable water, vault toilets, fire rings; $8/night single, first-come, first-served, open mid-May to early Nov. --Claude

name: Campo Alto Campground
note: Los Padres National Forest (Mt. Pinos Ranger District) atop Cerro Noroeste at ~8,250 ft; 15 single sites + 2 group sites, picnic tables/fire rings, vault toilet, no potable water or hookups; fits most modest-sized RVs and tents. Open May-Nov, reservable online (concessionaire-operated). Access via Cerro Noroeste Rd then Forest Rd 9N27. RV Life 0*(unrated)/1 $ sign (auto 7/2026). --Claude

name: Horton Creek Campground
note: BLM Bishop Field Office; 49 RV/tent sites (incl. 4 pull-throughs) at ~4,960 ft in Round Valley below the Eastern Sierra; max recommended RV length 30 ft, potable water, no hookups; $12/night, first-come, first-served (no reservations). Access via US-395 and South Round Valley Rd. Open May-Oct. RV Life 4*/1 $ sign (auto 7/2026). --Claude

name: Leapin' Lizard RV Ranch
note: Fenced desert RV resort near Ocotillo Wells / Anza-Borrego; 60 full-hookup (water/sewer/elec, cable, WiFi) big-rig-friendly sites, pool, heated spa, playground, laundry, showers; nightly plus full-season, online reservations; seasonal open ~Oct 1-Jun 1 (closed for summer heat). --Claude

name: Tecopa Hot Springs Resort
note: Privately-run Tecopa Hot Springs Resort & Campground (400 Tecopa Hot Springs Rd), near the SE approach to Death Valley; ~30 sites with 30/50-amp partial hookups plus 200+ dry sites, bathhouse with natural mineral hot-spring tubs, motel + cabins on site. Reservable; open ~Oct 1–Jun 1. --Claude

name: Summerdale Campground
note: Sierra NF (Bass Lake RD) campground on Hwy 41 ~1.5 mi south of Yosemite's south entrance near Fish Camp; ~29 sites with paved spurs along Big Creek, vault toilets, water, max RV 24 ft, no hookups. Reservable, open ~mid-May to mid-Sep. --Claude

name: Sherwin Creek Campground
note: Inyo NF campground ~2 mi from Mammoth Lakes along aspen-lined Sherwin Creek (elev ~7,600 ft); 87 sites, RVs to 60 ft (most 35-40), no hookups, water, vault toilets, RV fill station, bear lockers; Sherwin Lakes trailhead adjacent. Reservable, open ~mid-May to early Sep. --Claude

name: Old Shady Rest Campground (Inyo NF)
note: USFS campground in Jeffrey pine forest on the edge of Mammoth Lakes at ~7,800 ft. 51 non-hookup sites (dump station on site), sites listed for RVs/trailers roughly 18-58 ft. Reservable on recreation.gov; open ~May-Oct. --Claude

name: Brown's Owens River Campground
note: Family-run private campground in the meadow lining the upper Owens River near Bishop. 80+ dry (no-hookup) RV and tent sites — no hookups, no dump station; camp store, coin laundry, hot showers for guests. Open ~Apr-Sep. --Claude

name: Pine Cliff Resort
note: Long-running private RV park & campground among Jeffrey pines just above June Lake's beach in the Eastern Sierra. 200+ sites — full-hookup, partial and dry — plus general store, gas/propane, laundry, showers. Sites narrow with only a couple of pull-throughs for 38-ft rigs; a 23-ft rig fits. Reservable; open ~late Apr-Nov 1. --Claude

name: Hunewill's Doc and Al's Resort
note: Seasonal (late Apr–Oct) family RV resort on Robinson Creek in the Bridgeport/Twin Lakes area, Eastern Sierra. Back-in RV sites with hookups plus grassy campsites, fire rings, restrooms/showers; reservable with walk-ins when available; ~3 mi to Twin Lakes/Buckeye. --Claude

name: Topaz Lake RV Park
note: Private RV park on the west shore of Topaz Lake at the CA/NV line. ~54 full-hookup sites (water/sewer/electric), cable/wifi. Open Mar-Oct; drop-in overnighters welcome (reserve by phone/text). Transient RV park, not 55+/residential. --Claude

name: Fallen Leaf Campground
note: USFS Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit campground on the north shore of Fallen Leaf Lake near Taylor Creek, <1 mi from South Lake Tahoe. 206 sites (incl 6 yurts + standard tent/RV); RVs to 40 ft (trailers/5th-wheels to 30 ft). Reservable on recreation.gov; typically mid-May to mid-Oct. --Claude

name: Sycamore Ranch RV Park & Campground
note: Yuba County park on Hwy 20 near Browns Valley, along Dry Creek just upstream of the lower Yuba River (adjoins county's Hammon Grove Park). 28 RV/tent sites, all with water & electric hookups, paved pads, updated restrooms. Small-boat launch to Dry Creek. Open ~April-December; reservations required, online. --Claude

name: Lakeshore Resort at Bucks Lake
note: Private lakeside resort at 16001 Bucks Lake Rd, Quincy, on Bucks Lake (Plumas NF). ~50 camping sites (RV sites with water/sewer plus cabins), showers, on-site restaurant/bar and store at the water's edge. Seasonal (summer). --Claude  Bucks Lake drawn down below normal after Labor Day 2026 for dam repairs; boat ramps unusable from about mid-September 2026 (PG&E notice, 2026-10-10). --Claude

name: Haskins Valley Campground
note: PG&E-operated campground (utility-run = private per convention) on the south shore of Bucks Lake, 16731 Bucks Lake Rd, Quincy. 65 sites, no hookups, potable water, vault toilets, dump station; a few sites fit RVs up to 30 ft, most best for tents. Reservable through PG&E (2-night min); sites 10 and 14-29 are first-come, first-served. Open early June to early October. --Claude  Bucks Lake drawn down below normal after Labor Day 2026 for dam repairs; boat ramps unusable from about mid-September 2026 (PG&E notice, 2026-10-10). --Claude  Reservations need at least 2 nights; first-come, first-served sites can be taken for one night (PG&E, 2026-10-10). --Claude

name: Eagle Lake RV Park
note: Commercial RV park in the Spalding tract on Eagle Lake's SW shore (687-125 Palmetto Way / The Strand). ~90 sites incl 65 full hookups (30/50-amp) plus tent sites; big rigs to ~51 ft, 8 new lakeview FHU sites (2026); open ~May 1-Dec 1. Transient nightly, reservable. --Claude

name: Orman Guest Ranch & Stables
note: Family-run 67-acre ranch campground in woodland/pasture ~2 mi (about 250 yds through the woods) from the Pacific near Crescent City, a Redwood NP gateway; drive-in tent/RV/horse sites spread over the grounds, no hookups but water spigots, port-a-potties, coin showers, WiFi; seasonal (roughly May–Sep). General campground that also offers horse/stable sites. --Claude

name: Réserve faunique Rouge-Matawin – Camping Lac des Sucreries
note: Sépaq wildlife-reserve campground on Lac des Sucreries (La Macaza / south sector of Rouge-Matawin). Small rustic campground with semi-serviced and no-service drive-in sites (parking accessible by car), pit toilets and sanitary facilities in the sector, plus 4 ready-to-camp tents. Reservable online (semi-serviced season mid-May to late Oct). --Claude

name: Parc national du Mont-Orford — Camping Lac-Stukely
note: SEPAQ Parc national du Mont-Orford, Lac-Stukely sector: 148 serviced/semi-serviced drive-in sites (50 with electricity) in a hardwood forest; supervised beach, watercraft rental, dump station and wheelchair-accessible showers; FCFS bike-in sites in the Mélèze loop. Reservable online. Open mid-May to mid-Oct. --Claude

name: Parc national de la Yamaska — Camping
note: SEPAQ Parc national de la Yamaska on Réservoir Choinière: ~118-site campground with semi-serviced and 2-service (water+electricity) drive-in sites, plus rustic cyclist sites and ready-to-camp units; beach, bike path, dump/fill station. Non-potable water advisory in the camping sector (potable fill station at the beach pavilion). Reservable online. Open May to mid-Oct. --Claude

name: Parc national du Mont-Orford — Camping Lac-Fraser
note: SEPAQ Parc national du Mont-Orford, Lac-Fraser sector: 149 serviced/semi-serviced drive-in sites (many with electricity) in a deciduous forest; supervised beach, watercraft rental, laundry and central dump station. Reservable online. Open mid-May to mid-Oct. --Claude

name: Réserve faunique Mastigouche — Camping Lac Saint-Bernard
note: SEPAQ Réserve faunique Mastigouche, Camping du Lac-Saint-Bernard (two sections on Lac Saint-Bernard): ~100 sites — 73 semi-serviced + 16 with water — plus Hékipia tents; sandy beach, playground, community hall, convenience store, dump station. Semi-serviced pads ~25 ft accept camping vans and small motorhomes (site 61 is 25 x 30 ft). RV/trailer campers should enter via the Pins-Rouges registration centre. Extended season to mid-Oct. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Camping Lac Chigoubiche (Réserve faunique Ashuapmushuan)
note: SEPAQ Réserve faunique Ashuapmushuan (provincial, not federal). Camping Lac-Chigoubiche at km 113 Route 167, 34 drive-in sites on Lac Chigoubiche with sanitary block, hot showers and dumping station; accommodates RVs (operator lists rigs over 35 ft allowed). Reservable via SEPAQ; open late May–Oct. --Claude

name: Camping Le Bleuvet (Parc national du Fjord-du-Saguenay)
note: SEPAQ parc national du Fjord-du-Saguenay (Quebec provincial), Baie-Sainte-Marguerite sector, 1121 Route 172 Nord, Sacré-Coeur. ~50–60 drive-in sites, semi-serviced or water+electric, level and spacious, accommodating tents and RVs; wooded loops set back from the Sainte-Marguerite river/bay. Reservable via SEPAQ; open late May–mid-Oct. --Claude

name: Camping Pied-des-Monts (Parc national des Grands-Jardins)
note: SEPAQ parc national des Grands-Jardins (Quebec provincial), Pied-des-Monts campground near the Route 381 park entrance: 27 semi-serviced sites plus 9 with electricity, drive-in for RVs. Reservable via SEPAQ; mid-May to mid-Oct. --Claude

name: Camping Lac Arthabaska (Parc national des Grands-Jardins)
note: SEPAQ parc national des Grands-Jardins (Quebec provincial), Camping Lac Arthabaska near the Arthabaska discovery/service centre: 30 semi-serviced drive-in sites (offered as rustic sans-service early and late season) on Lac Arthabaska; car-accessible in the heart of the park. Reservable via SEPAQ; mid-May to mid-Oct. --Claude

name: Réserve faunique de Matane – Camping Étang-à-la-Truite
note: Réserve faunique de Matane. 21 serviced/semi-serviced drive-in sites on Étang à la Truite, 42 km from the John registration centre via a car-accessible gravel road; sanitary block w/ showers. Isolated, shaded, lake-view sites; open late May–early Sept, reservable via SEPAQ. RV Life 0* (unrated)/$ (auto 6/2026). --Claude

name: Réserve faunique de Matane – Camping John
note: Réserve faunique de Matane, at the John registration centre near the reserve's main road. 24 serviced/semi-serviced drive-in sites, mostly sunny and close together; sanitary block w/ showers. Open late May–early Sept, reservable via SEPAQ. RV Life 0* (unrated)/$ (auto 6/2026). --Claude

name: Camping municipal et marina de Brownsburg-Chatham
note: Municipal campground of the Ville de Brownsburg-Chatham on the Ottawa River (rivière des Outaouais) with a 200-slip marina, boat launch and swimming beach; ~245 sites, 166 with 3 services and 79 with 2 services. Open late Apr–mid-Oct; takes nightly campers, reservable. --Claude

name: Mill Dam Park
note: Small municipal park in Shawville (village of Shawville / MRC de Pontiac) on a creek/mill-dam with ~6 full-service drive-in RV sites (water + electric) at $20/night, plus free tent camping (3 nights); toilets, dump station ($5), spring water, splash pad. First-come, first-served (reservations allowed only for the Shawville Fair weekend). Open May–Oct. --Claude

name: Camping Sainte-Véronique
note: Municipal campground managed by the Ville de Rivière-Rouge since 1986, on Lac Tibériade and the Jourdain River in the Hautes-Laurentides; ~200 sites with 2 or 3 services plus rustic sites, swimming beach, fishing. Open mid-May–mid-Oct, reservable. --Claude

name: Camping du Parc de l'Île Melville
note: Municipal nonprofit outdoor park (Parc de l'Île Melville) in Shawinigan, along the Saint-Maurice River; 152 sites — 107 with 3 services, 14 water/electric, 24 unserviced — plus 6 cabins, pool, boat launch, trails. Open early May–mid-Oct, reservable. --Claude

name: Centre de plein air de Beauport
note: Municipal campground run by the Ville de Québec (Centre de plein air de Beauport, formerly Camping municipal de Beauport) near the Montmorency River; 136 sites, 54 with 3 services, 30-amp electric/water/dump station, pool, trails. Open early June–Labour Day, reservable via campin.ca. --Claude

name: Camping régional de Malartic
note: Town-run campground operated by the Ville de Malartic, ~2 km from downtown in Abitibi-Témiscamingue. Serviced and unserviced drive-in RV sites plus 4 small chalets, dumping station, heated pool, playgrounds; open ~late May to mid-Sep. Reservable. --Claude

name: Éco-Camping de Chibougamau
note: Beside Lac Sauvage south of Chibougamau (Rte 167 S), operated by FaunENord, a regional nonprofit outdoor organization. 44 drive-in sites with 0/2/3 services (30-amp electricity), showers, laundry, dump station; direct trail access to Parc Obalski. Reservable online or by phone; open ~mid-May to early Sep. --Claude

name: Camping Jonquière
note: On the shore of Lac Kénogami at Lac-Kénogami (Ville de Saguenay), ~10 km from downtown Jonquière. Nonprofit-run (Camping Jonquière inc.) on municipal public land, est. 1980; ~270 sites, 200+ with services incl. ~40 pull-through/motorhome sites, plus a 70-slip marina, boat launch, municipal beach and restaurant. Reservable; open summer season. --Claude

name: Halte VR Pointe-Scott (Roberval)
note: Free municipal RV halte run by the Ville de Roberval on Pointe-Scott, jutting into Lac Saint-Jean beside the municipal beach. ~35 designated RV/trailer spaces (no tents), overnight allowed, with toilets, a dump station and potable water for filling tanks. First-come, first-served; free with a suggested voluntary contribution. Seasonal. --Claude

name: Camping municipal de la Pointe (Rivière-du-Loup)
note: Municipal campground at 2 côte des Bains, Rivière-du-Loup, on Parc de la Pointe overlooking the St. Lawrence estuary. ~113 sites, many full-hookup, with dump station, sanitary blocks, showers, laundry, Wi-Fi and a water playground. Reservable; open ~May to Oct. --Claude

name: Camping Camp d'Accueil (Lac Ha! Ha!)
note: Community/municipal camp on the shore of Lac Ha! Ha! (RV Life mis-tags the city as Saint-Urbain; it is actually in Ferland-et-Boilleau), founded 50+ years ago by the municipality's citizens' committee. ~44 drive-in sites, rustic (tap water/showers, largely no electrical hookups); accepts RVs/trailers, visible on satellite. Season late May–mid-Sept, reservable online. --Claude

name: Camping Municipal l'Oasis
note: Municipal campground of Saint-David-de-Falardeau on Lac Clair (694 Chemin du Lac-Emmuraillé); 65 sites, mix of no-service and three-service (30-amp) sites, boat ramp, beach access, laundry. Season ~May 22–Sept 13, reservable online. --Claude

name: Camping Municipal Le Paradis
note: Municipal campground of Port-Cartier along the Rivière Dominique downtown (Boulevard du Portage-des-Mousses); 39 sites — 12 no-service, 2 water/elec, 25 three-service (30-amp) — community hall, showers, laundry, municipal bike-path access. Season late May–mid-Oct, reservable online. --Claude

name: Camping de la Plage
note: Riverfront family campground on the Rivière Rouge off Route 117 S in Rivière-Rouge; 72 drive-in sites (about 46 transient / 26 seasonal) with or without electricity, plus 1 chalet; sand beach, canoe/kayak/SUP access. Operated by the Société de développement commercial de Rivière-Rouge. Open ~May–Sept, reservable online (official site cert currently expired). --Claude

name: Camping de Compton
note: Family RV campground ~20 min south of Sherbrooke (Cantons-de-l'Est), two sectors (Hatley + La Station); ~300 drive-in sites, 15/30/50-amp electric, water & sewer hookups, accepts RVs up to ~50 ft; pool, dump station. Nightly transient reservable online. Open mid-Apr–late Oct. --Claude

name: Camping St-Joseph-de-Beauce
note: Family-owned campground (~70 sites) along the Rivière des Fermes in the Beauce; 30-amp electric hookups, water, heated pool, service pavilion, laundry, river swimming/fishing access. Season ~May–mid-Oct; reservations by phone. --Claude

name: Camping des Sillons
note: Coastal campground (~125 grass sites) on Île du Havre aux Maisons, Îles-de-la-Madeleine, bordering the Dune-du-Sud beach on the Gulf of St. Lawrence. Serviced (15/20/30/50-amp, water, some sewer) and unserviced sites, dump station, showers, Wi-Fi. Season ~Jun–Sep; reservable. --Claude

name: Camping du Quai
note: Large RV-oriented campground (150+ sites) at Rivière-du-Loup near the St. Lawrence estuary; pull-through sites with 30/50-amp 2–3-service hookups, heated pool, splash pad, gym, store. Season ~May–Oct; reservable online. --Claude

name: Camping Cabano
note: Campground (~150 sites) in the Cabano quarter of Témiscouata-sur-le-Lac, exit 40 off Hwy 85/185, marketed as a traveler stopover to the Maritimes/Gaspésie; 15/30-amp electric, dump station, hot showers, laundry, pool, trail network near Lac Témiscouata. Season ~Apr–Oct; operating (own site campingcabano.com currently under construction). --Claude

name: Camping de l'Anse
note: Municipally-owned campground (~50+ sites) at L'Anse-Saint-Jean on the Saguenay fjord, at the mouth of the Rivière Saint-Jean; most sites ~1,500 sq ft with 3 services (water/electric/sewer), heated pool, mini-golf, playground, hot showers. Gateway to fjord kayaking. Season ~mid-May–mid-Oct; reservable. Owned by the municipality of L'Anse-Saint-Jean. --Claude

name: Camping Capitaine Homard
note: Shoreline campground on the St. Lawrence at Sainte-Flavie (gateway to the Gaspe peninsula). ~53 sites, majority 3-service (30 amp), several facing the sea; dump station, laundry, on-site restaurant. Open roughly May-Oct. --Claude

name: Camping de la Mer
note: Large beachfront campground on the St. Lawrence at Pointe-Lebel (Baie-Comeau, Cote-Nord). 306 sites with & without services incl. 30/50-amp water+sewer full-service; daily transient rates plus seasonal; beach, boat launch/marina. Open roughly mid-May to mid-Oct. --Claude

name: Camping Chutes aux Iroquois
note: Private RV campground (Camping Union – Chutes-aux-Iroquois), ~170 sites on the Rivière Rouge near Mont-Tremblant/Labelle; open May–Oct. Serviced (30A, water/sewer) and unserviced drive-in sites incl pull-throughs for big rigs, plus cabins/chalets; sandy beach, pool, dump station. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Camping Trans-Canadien
note: Large family-run private park (~300 sites, operating ~30 yrs) on the Ottawa River (Lac des Deux-Montagnes) at Rigaud, ~40 min W of Montreal; open May–Oct. Many seasonal sites but takes nightly transient RVs — full hookups (30/50A, water/sewer), pull-throughs, max ~55 ft; pool, dump station. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Camping Lac Lafontaine
note: Parkbridge RV park on Lac Lafontaine in Saint-Jérôme (Laurentians), 355 sites ~30-45 min from Montreal. Dedicated 'terrains voyageurs' (nightly transient) 2- and 3-service sites, 30/50-amp, plus rustic lakeshore tent sites and a few cabins; pool, lake access, restaurant; season ~late Apr-late Oct. --Claude

name: Parc de Motorisés Godefroy
note: Motorhome-only RV park (Class A/B/C) between the fleuve Saint-Laurent and Godefroy golf course; 19 full-service drive-in sites (30/50A, water, sewer), 30'x80' pads with cedar-hedge privacy, dump station, free WiFi; open ~mid-Apr–mid-Oct, reservable (nightly transient). --Claude

name: Camping Beau-Lieu
note: Large family campground (~696 sites, mostly seasonal) 10 min from downtown Sherbrooke on the Route verte bike path; reserves transient/passage sites near the on-site pond for travelers; 30/50A + full hookups, pull-through, max RV ~45 ft, restaurant, 2 pools, dump station; open ~late-Apr–early-Oct. --Claude

name: Camping Plage Kirkland
note: Long-established (60+ yr) beach campground on Baie Missisquoi / Lac Champlain in Venise-en-Québec; ~166 grassy drive-in sites with 30A electric (water/sewer on some), private beach, pool, dump station, boat rentals; nightly transient reservable, open ~May–Sept. --Claude

name: Camping Le Marquis
note: Family campground on the fleuve Saint-Laurent in Saint-Sulpice (Lanaudière); ~165 sites, 161 with 3 services (30/50A, water, sewer), heated pool, mini-golf, dump station; nightly transient reservable, open ~mid-May–mid-Sept. --Claude

name: Camping Stoneham
note: Well-equipped campground in Stoneham-et-Tewkesbury, ~20 km N of Québec City near Parc de la Jacques-Cartier; ~259 sites with and without services (full hookups available), on-site pond, heated pool, store, mini-golf; promoted as a road-trip stopover (nightly transient), open ~mid-May–mid-Sept. --Claude

name: Camping au Plateau 5 Étoiles
note: Large family RV park in Terrebonne (1770 Côte de Terrebonne) near the Rivière des Mille Îles, ~15 min from Montréal. ~222 RV sites, predominantly seasonal but keeps a dedicated 3-service traveler section (full hookups 30/50A, ~8 pull-throughs) bookable nightly (Good Sam lists a nightly rate); heated pool, hot tub, sauna, organized activities. Open mid-Apr to mid-Oct; reservable online. --Claude

name: Camping Lac Saint-Michel
note: Camping Union - Lac St-Michel, ~15 min from downtown Trois-Rivières, built on two levels along the Saint-Maurice River. ~155 varied drive-in sites (~60 full hookups, ~20 pull-throughs), accepts big rigs to ~60 ft, RV dump on site; 'Express overnight' transient bookings plus chalets/ready-to-camp. On-site 20 m pool and artificial lake. Open ~May–mid-Sep; reservable online. --Claude

name: Camping Un Air d'Été
note: Private family campground at 459 Rte Grand Capsa, Pont-Rouge (35 km W of Québec City). Serviced + unserviced drive-in RV sites plus prêt-à-camper and cabin rentals; standard sites take trailers to ~25 ft, 30A sites to 26–32 ft. On-site swim lake, heated pool, near Jacques-Cartier River. Open mid-May–late Sept; reservable online. --Claude

name: Camping Plage Champlain
note: Private campground on the shore of Lake Champlain at Venise-en-Québec (Montérégie), 192 sites. Offers both voyageur (nightly) and seasonal sites: unserviced $56, 2-service (15A) $61, 3-service (30A) $66/night; drive-in RV sites to ~39 ft. Laundry, showers, dump station, gated. Open mid-May–mid-Sept. --Claude

name: Camping Pointe-aux-Oies de Montmagny
note: Municipal campground (Ville de Montmagny — the city's own site posts its news/classification) at 45 av. du Bassin Nord on the St. Lawrence River shore, Chaudière-Appalaches. 311 drive-in sites + 3 yurts, 30 & 50A service, water park, bike path to downtown; 5-star Québec classification. Open mid-May–mid-Oct; reservable online. --Claude

name: Camping Mont-Sainte-Anne
note: Private campground run by the Mont-Sainte-Anne resort at 300 rang Saint-Julien, Saint-Férréol-les-Neiges (~30 min NE of Québec City). 166 large wooded drive-in sites — no-service, 2-service, or 3-service (48 sites full-service) — plus prêt-à-camper; on-site lake with beach. Open ~mid-May–mid-Oct; reservable by phone. --Claude

name: Camping Domaine Champêtre
note: Private family campground in the Bellechasse countryside near Lévis/Québec City; ~208 sites over varying service levels incl. 30/50-amp full-hookup RV sites, dump station, pool, playground; open mid-May to mid-Sept, reservable online. Inland farm setting, no water body on site. --Claude

name: Camping Tadoussac
note: Campground operated by Vacances Essipit (Innu First Nation of Essipit), perched on a mountainside above the mouth of the Saguenay Fjord / St. Lawrence; 193 tent/RV sites (accepts rigs over 35 ft) plus a few ready-to-camp and chalets; open mid-May to late Sept, reservable online/by phone. --Claude

name: Camping Bon-Désir
note: Municipal campground owned/operated by the Municipality of Les Bergeronnes on a 40-ha site in the Saguenay–St. Lawrence Marine Park (whale-watching coast); ~153 sites incl. ~78 near the St. Lawrence estuary shore; open mid-May to mid-Oct, reservable online. --Claude

name: Camping du Phare à Percé
note: Private seaside campground on the cliff top ~3 min west of downtown Percé, route 132; ~120-140 sites incl 66 full-hookup plus electric-only and elec+water, 15/30/50-amp service, accepts large RVs (advertised to ~55 ft). Cliffside/oceanfront sites overlook Percé Rock and Île Bonaventure. Reservable online. Open early June-Sept. --Claude

name: Nature Océan Chalets - Camping
note: Private campground on a 40-acre rolling seaside property on route 132 west of Percé, panoramic view of Percé Rock, Île Bonaventure and the ocean. 159 sites, electricity 15/30 amp, mix of RV/tent sites plus chalets; dump station, showers, laundry. Reservable. Open June-early Oct. --Claude

name: Camping Baie de Gaspé
note: Private campground at Cap-aux-Os on the Baie de Gaspé, ~20 min from Gaspé and adjacent to Forillon NP. 144 sites incl 128 with 3 services (30/50-amp elec/water/sewer) plus 13 unserviced; chalets/motel also on site. Dump station, showers, Wi-Fi. Reservable. Open late May-late Sept. --Claude

name: Camping des Appalaches
note: Private family campground on the banks of the Rivière Morris near Rivière-au-Renard, ~15 min from Gaspé and 45 min from Percé Rock. 180 sites; accepts tents through Class B/C motorhomes and trailers; showers, dump station. Reservable. Open June-Sept. --Claude

name: Algonquin Pines Campground
note: Family campground on Hwy 60 at Dwight, about 20 km west of Algonquin Provincial Park's West Gate and 23 km from Huntsville. Listed at 143 drive-in sites — 43 pull-throughs, 15 full-hookup and 98 hydro/water sites on 15/30 amp — plus glamping tents and a cabin. Washroom/shower buildings, coin laundry, camp store, dump station, pool, mini-putt, playground and covered pavilion. Open Victoria Day long weekend to Thanksgiving. --Claude

name: Brennan Harbour RV Park
note: Small owner-operated RV park on Bushwell Bay off the North Channel of Georgian Bay (Lake Huron), east of Spanish. 42 sites, all with metered 30/50-amp hydro, water and full sewer (pump-out); back-ins listed to 50 ft; shaded, sunny and water-front sites plus limited boat dockage. Site mix is mostly leased seasonal, but the operator's rate sheet explicitly lists 'transient sites available' with 30/50-amp hydro and water at $60-80 CAD daily ($360-480 weekly), so nightly RV camping is a standing product. No tents allowed; RV/trailer units older than 15 years may be refused. Open early May to mid-October (Thanksgiving). Book by phone/email reservation form; no online booking engine. --Claude

name: Crystal Lake Campground
note: Small privately-owned campground on Crystal Lake, 6 km west of Vermilion Bay and about 1 km south of Hwy 17 on Hanslips Rd. 28 numbered sites plus a group site: 5 full-service pull-thrus, 8 full-service back-ins, 12 electrical (15 amp) and 2 unserviced; seasonal sites only by approval, so the inventory is essentially transient. 2026 nightly rates $42-60 CAD; cash on arrival, reservations by email preferred. Season roughly June 1 to fall (site posted a June 1, 2026 reopening). Sandy beach, playground, nature trail, canoe/kayak/bike rentals, WiFi. --Claude

name: Davy Lake Campground & Resort
note: Family-run (since 2005) campground on Davy Lake just off Trans-Canada Hwy 17 at Ignace. Roughly 50-65 sites — grassy back-ins and pull-thrus, about 21 full hookup (water/sewer/30-50 amp) and 14 electric+water, plus cabins and rental trailers; nightly transient camping is the main business. Open mid-May to end of September; reservable online through Good Sam Booking or by phone (807-934-0914 in season). Nightly rates roughly $40-105 CAD by site type. Sandy beach, swim dock, store, laundry, dump station, 70+ acres of trails. --Claude

name: Glengarry Campground
note: St. Lawrence Parks Commission (Parks of the St. Lawrence, an agency of the Government of Ontario) campground on Lake St. Francis / the St. Lawrence River at Lancaster — RV Life mistags it commercial. 170+ drive-in sites in old-growth pine: regular, electric-only and recreation-vehicle sites plus premium waterfront sites and roofed accommodation; gravel pads, bass and perch fishing, views across to the Adirondacks. Open ~late May to mid-October; reservable online. --Claude

name: Happy Hearts Tent & Trailer Park
note: 25-acre family park on Cape Hurd Road just outside Tobermory at the tip of the Bruce Peninsula — a base for Bruce Peninsula National Park and Fathom Five. ~133 sites on back-in gravel pads taking everything from pop-ups to large motorhomes, with 15/30/50-amp + water sites and some 30-amp water/sewer sites (24 full hookups) plus a dump station; pool, playground, laundry, hot showers. Overnight camping plus a May-Oct seasonal section; reserve by phone or online. --Claude

name: Linamac Lodge & Trailer Park
note: 40-acre partially wooded campground on Lake Louise, on Hwy 129 about 20 km (15 minutes) south of Chapleau. Over 50 full-service sites offered for overnight, weekly or seasonal use, all with drinking water, 30-50 amp electric, septic, fire pit and picnic table; drive-through sites suit motorhomes and trailers, plus tent areas and housekeeping cabins. Renovated shower house, game room, camp shop, playground, private sandy beach with paddle boats, kayaks, SUPs and a floating trampoline; ATV and logging-road trails from the property. Open mid-May to mid-October, weather permitting; reserve by phone or email. --Claude

name: Lower Beverley Lake Park
note: Township-owned, board-run municipal park of the Township of Rideau Lakes on Lower Beverley Lake at Delta; 235 trailer and tent campsites plus 11 cottages and 2 bunkies on 106 acres. Non-serviced, 30-amp and 50-amp serviced sites; 2026 nightly rates $38.25 non-serviced / $63.25 30-amp / $70.25 50-amp CAD plus tax. Beach, playground, ball diamond, laundry, showers. Open Friday of Mother's Day weekend to Thanksgiving weekend in October; reservations by request form or phone. --Claude

name: Mountain Lake Camp
note: Family camp at 102 Mountain Lake Drive, 11 km southeast of Wiarton on Mountain Lake (Bruce Peninsula). Heavily seasonal - 105 fully serviced seasonal sites with 30-amp power, running water, sewage holding tank and fire pit - but the operator also runs a separate transient/weekend area of roughly 14 sites for RVs, trailers and tents with published nightly rates of $60 trailer/RV and $45 tent CAD plus HST. Five housekeeping cottages, in-ground pool, playground. Open May long weekend to Thanksgiving long weekend; book by phone or email. --Claude

name: Oasis RV Resort
note: Modern full-hookup RV park on 50 acres beside the Calypso waterpark at Limoges, about 25 minutes east of Ottawa off Highway 417; open roughly mid-May to mid-October. Spacious gravel back-in sites with water, electric and sewer, plus rustic and glamping cabins; mini golf, heated salt-water pool, petting zoo, jump pillow, playground, on-site canteen and bar, laundry, dog park. Nightly rates from about $69; reservable online. --Claude

name: Ivy Lea Campground
note: Managed by the St. Lawrence Parks Commission, an agency of the Government of Ontario, on the Thousand Islands Parkway at Lansdowne in the heart of the 1000 Islands. 140+ campsites: 41 RV sites with water and 30 amp service, 27 premium waterfront unserviced sites, 74 regular unserviced sites, 4 walk-in wilderness sites and 4 camper cabins; trailer dump station, comfort station with showers, laundromat, food concession, beach, playground, boat launch and dock rentals. Campers receive a free pass to Upper Canada Village or Fort Henry during the main season (mid-May to Labour Day). Reservable online. --Claude

name: Port Glasgow Trailer Park
note: Municipality of West Elgin campground on the Lake Erie bluff at Port Glasgow, ~20 acres of seasonal lots plus a dedicated block of 24 transient sites for tents or trailers. Municipal transient-site page lists nightly rates of $51 tent, $69 hydro+water and $74 hydro+water+sewer (weekly $374/$411), so serviced drive-in sites are available to overnighters. Open May to October. Book by calling or emailing the municipal office (ext. 244); payment on arrival. --Claude

name: Redden's Camp
note: Full-service camp on Longbow Lake (Lake of the Woods watershed) at 4433 Hwy 17 E southeast of Kenora, formerly Longbow Lake Campground. Mix of seasonal sites, cabins and a transient block of 9 overnight RV sites with full-service hookups (30 amp, water, sewer); 2026 nightly rates $47, or $52 for the premium lakeside sites 141 and 142. Season opens May 8; comfort stations with showers and laundry, on-site store, marina/boat launch, two private beaches. Reserve online or by phone with a one-night deposit. --Claude

name: Rock Island Camp & RV Park
note: 180-acre wooded campground on rolling granite between Athens and Mallorytown (Front of Yonge Twp). Camping in Ontario's operator listing breaks the inventory down as 48 overnight RV sites, 15 overnight tent sites and 62 full-season sites, max RV length 45 ft, 30-amp service; operator rates page posts nightly rates of $52 (no hydro) / $56 (with hydro), weekly and monthly rates, with mobile water fill and pump-out sold separately rather than site sewer. Open May 1 - mid-October. Reserve by request form or phone (one night charged to hold the site). --Claude

name: Smith's Trailer Park & Camp
season_source: note prose (cleaned out of the note 2026-10-14)
note: Long-running family park (in operation over 90 years) on the east shore of Little Lake in Midland, minutes from town. 147 sites split between a fully-booked seasonal section and an overnight section; the operator's site map shows numbered loops on Stan's Circle, Minnow/Catfish/Perch/Bass Drives and Lakeshore Road with 30-amp and 50-amp electric, water and sewer, paved roads and gravel pads, plus pull-thrus.  No tent camping.  Beach on Little Lake, pool, store, propane, laundry, playground.  Overnight season runs mid-May to October; reservations through CampLife.  A separate mobile-home park adjoins the campground at the office end. --Claude

name: Tiny Village Ottawa River
note: Private 59-acre campground at 34572 Hwy 17, Deep River, on the Ottawa River with ~2,000 ft of sandy beach. Offers transient RV sites (max ~40 ft) with electric+water or water-only hookups, plus tent and glamping sites; nightly rate ~$55, open mid-May to mid-Oct. --Claude

name: Tiny Village Woodland
note: Private 96-acre campground (formerly Woodland Park Arden) at 1111 Woodland Park Dr, Central Frontenac, on a bay of Bull Lake with ~300 ft sandy beach. ~75 serviced sites (70 electric+water, 5 electric-only, 30-amp, max ~40 ft) including Beach RV sites, plus unserviced/tent and cabins; overnight and seasonal, open mid-May to mid-Oct. --Claude

name: Tomahawk RV Campground
note: Private resort RV park at Sioux Narrows on Lake of the Woods. Full-hookup sites (water/electric/sewer, 50-amp) with pull-thrus and big-rig access, sandy beach, boat docks; nightly rate $44-52 plus weekly/monthly/seasonal, open mid-May to mid-Oct. Satellite confirms a lakeside resort with docks. --Claude

name: Willow Grove Family Campground
note: Family-run private campground on former farmland ~10 km east of Bashaw on Hwy 53, then 1.5 km north (42102 Range Road 204); operating since 1988. Fully serviced sites with power, water and sewer, free showers, heated pool, rec room, laundry, convenience store, playgrounds/pickleball. Mostly seasonal (150+ sites, waitlisted) but holds a real transient inventory of 20+ weekender sites bookable nightly. Open May long weekend to Thanksgiving; reservations strongly recommended. --Claude

name: Point Wolfe Campground
note: Fundy NP coastal campground ~8 km west of the east entrance, reached across the Point Wolfe covered bridge — max vehicle/equipment length 7.3 m (24 ft) and height 4.4 m (13 ft), so a 23-ft rig fits. 155 drive-in sites: 24 electric/water, 120 unserviced (+10 oTENTiks, 1 Ôasis). Washrooms/showers, dump station; cell reception extremely limited. Reservable, open ~late June to early Sept. --Claude

name: Campbellton RV Camping
note: City of Campbellton municipal campground at the Restigouche River Experience Centre (1 Riverview Dr); ~86 fully/electrical-serviced drive-in sites incl pull-thrus, dump station, showers, laundry, WiFi. Transient nightly. Open late May-late Sep. --Claude

name: South Cove Camping & Golf
note: Private campground + 9-hole golf in Shediac; 150+ full-service & tenting sites, pull-throughs (reserved for 31 ft+) with 50/30-amp. Full-service $65-70, W/E $50, unserviced $40 nightly plus seasonal — nightly transient confirmed. Low-season rates open–Jun 15 & Sep 15–Oct 13. --Claude

name: Inverness Beach Village

season.note: Mid-May to mid-October.

season_source: https://www.invernessbeachvillage.com/terms-conditions ('Our Season is Mid-May to Mid-October'), read 2026-10-13
note: Cottage and campground village on the outskirts of Inverness, above the sandy shores of the Gulf of St. Lawrence between two world-class golf courses, with private beach access, ocean sunsets and the Cabot Trail at its back door; the MacLeod family has run it since 1985.  Its unserviced sites take tents, pop-ups, teardrops, truck campers and small camper vans (18 ft), but no motor homes, RVs or travel trailers, and a site can be locked.  Tents aren't allowed on RV sites.  Wi-Fi is in the cottages but not on the campsites, and ATV stays need the village's approval, 4 at most at a time.  It also has 41 housekeeping cottages. --Claude

name: Arm of Gold Campground & RV Park
note: Private campground at 24 Church Road, Little Bras d'Or, ~5 min from the North Sydney Newfoundland ferry terminal; ~140 sites with full hookups (30/50-amp), pull-throughs for big rigs, washrooms/laundry, walking trail. Marketed for nightly transient/en-route stays. Satellite shows drive-in RV loops on open ground west of the Hwy 105 junction. Open seasonal (summer). --Claude

name: Riversedge Campground
note: Private riverside campground on the St. Mary's River just outside Sherbrooke village; satellite shows an open loop with drive-in RV/trailer pads and pull-offs along the west riverbank. Listed as an affordable RV campground; open seasonally. Site-level hookup detail not confirmed (operator site is a JS SPA, unreadable at audit). --Claude

name: Cedar Dunes Provincial Park
note: PEI provincial park on the Northumberland Strait at West Point (North Cape Coastal Drive), beside the West Point Lighthouse. 80 drive-in sites: 23 full-hookup, 46 electric+water, 11 unserviced; laundromat, dump station, washrooms with showers, WiFi. Reservable via PEI Parks. Open late June-late Sept. --Claude

name: Notre Dame Provincial Park
note: Parks NL provincial park at Lewisporte in central Newfoundland, on the shore of Junction Pond in boreal forest. 100 drive-in campsites, most accommodating larger RVs; 36 sites with 15/30/50A electrical; freshwater pond with a sandy beach for swimming/canoeing/angling. Open seasonal; reservable online via ParksNL. --Claude

name: Wilsonville Recreation Area

season.note: Camping season: the last Sunday in April to the third Sunday in October.

season_source: https://www.wilsonvillecampground1.com/contact/3690931 ('Our Camping Season is the Last Sunday in April Till the 3rd. Sunday in October'), read 2026-10-20
note: Largest of the Lake Wallenpaupack recreation areas, on a wooded point off US 6 at 113 Ammon Dr; the lake and its recreation areas are owned and run by utility operator Brookfield Renewable (formerly PPL), so it is a utility park rather than a government one. 160 tent and trailer sites with camp store, showers, laundry, dump station, playground, marina with rental slips, gas dock and boat ramps. The operator's colour site map classes sites as seasonal, 7-night-minimum, or 2-night-minimum (3 nights on holidays), so a large transient block is bookable; seasonal sites are currently full. 2026 rates $45/night RV or trailer, $38 tent, 15% off at 30+ nights, 30-night maximum stay. Camping season runs the last Sunday in April to the third Sunday in October. Electric and water reach at least part of the loop (a dated firsthand review reports 30A and water at site 41). No online booking - mail-in reservation form from Jan 1, phone reservations from Apr 25. No pets permitted, and swimming is not allowed within the recreation area. The older wilsonvillecampground.com domain now serves an expired certificate; wilsonvillecampground1.com is the live site. RV Life 4.5*/$$ ~$40/night (auto 9/2026). --Claude  MINIMUM STAY: 2 nights on reservations (7 at some sites), 3 on summer holiday weekends; first-come stays from 1 night (wilsonvillecampground1.com, 2026-10-12). --Claude

name: Badlands Hotel & Campground
note: Hotel plus campground on SD-377 at the edge of Interior, a mile from the Badlands NP entrance - the closest full-service base to the park's south side. About 80 level gravel pull-through sites with full hookups at 50/30 amp (plus 30-amp full-hookup and primitive/tent options) among roughly 100 total; two bathhouses, guest laundry, restaurant, store, pool and free wifi. Open May through September. Formerly Badlands Interior Motel & Campground. Priced above the sweep's usual private gate. RV Life 4*/$$$ (auto 9/2026)

name: Big Pine Campground

season.note: Open May to October; the operator publishes the months but no exact dates, so none are recorded.

note: Quiet, wooded campground off US-16 west of Custer, set back from highway noise under tall ponderosa. 50- and 30-amp full-hookup sites, water-and-electric, primitive and tent sites, camper cabins and a retro trailer rental; two bath houses, laundry, game room, RV supplies, free wifi. Open May to October, with a two-night deposit required over the Sturgis Rally dates. Priced above the sweep's usual private gate. RV Life 4.5*/$$$ (auto 9/2026)

name: Elk Creek Campground (Conejos River)

season.note: Memorial Day to Labor Day weekends (FS). Closed for the 2026 season; reopens Memorial Day weekend 2027.

season_source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/riogrande/recreation/elk-creek-campground ('Seasons of Use: Memorial Day to Labor Day weekends'; 'Closed for the season- Will resume Memorial Day weekend 2027'), read 2026-10-28
note: Lower Conejos Canyon near Horca, just off Hwy 17 (~23 mi west of Antonito), ~8,500 ft. Lightly wooded with spruce and some ponderosa over grass; a few sites sit next to Elk Creek, with public access to the creek and the Conejos River. Convenient to the South San Juan Wilderness (Elk Creek and Duck Lake trailheads). --Claude

name: Lake Fork Campground (Conejos River)

season.note: Memorial Day to Labor Day weekends (FS), with a cheaper shoulder season either side; FR 250 has an annual seasonal closure March 15 - May 15.

season_source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/riogrande/recreation/lake-fork-campground ('Seasons of Use: Memorial Day to Labor Day weekends'; 'Single Site: $10 per night (during shoulder season)'; 'annual seasonal road closures from March 15th to May 15th'), read 2026-10-28
note: Rio Grande NF campground on the Conejos River (Gold Medal trout water) in upper Conejos Canyon at ~9,500 ft, 17.5 mi up dirt FR 250 from CO 17, below Platoro; aspen and mixed conifers, some sites overlooking the river. --Claude Oct 2026: the Rio Grande NF conditions page says 'FSR 250 between Stunner to Highway 17 has damage - 4WD is recommended' after the October storm; check road status before going. --Claude 2026-10-28

name: Mill Creek Campground (Lake Fork Gunnison)

season.note: BLM: 'The campground is accessible June through September.' Reservations run Memorial Day to Sept 30.

season_source: https://www.blm.gov/visit/mill-creek-campground-co ('The campground is accessible June through September'; 'RESERVABLE up to 180-days in advance during peak season, Memorial Day through September 30th'), read 2026-10-28
note: BLM (Gunnison Field Office), 14 mi SW of Lake City at 9,500 ft, across a bridge from Cinnamon Pass Rd (CR 30) on the Lake Fork of the Gunnison. Shaded sites in spruce-fir and aspen; a fishing access trail leads to the river. Base camp for the Alpine Loop Backcountry Byway, which is for licensed OHVs and high-clearance 4WD beyond the campground. --Claude

name: Sandy Cove (Canton Lake)
note: Corps of Engineers campground at the north end of Canton Dam, 5 miles from Canton, in blackjack and post oak shade near a large swim beach. 35 sites with 30-amp electric (published 20-42 ft); water from shared hydrants (bring a Y and up to 100 ft of hose), no sewer and no dump station (the nearest is at Canadian campground). Showers, flush toilets. Closed November-March. Reservable online; 2-night minimum during the May Walleye Rodeo. --Claude

name: Macks Creek Campground (Lucky Peak Lake)
note: Small Corps of Engineers campground on Lucky Peak Lake, 25 miles from Boise via Highway 21 and Arrowrock Road. 5 RV/trailer sites (35-45 ft) above the road and 9 tent sites on the shore; shared boat docks and a ramp. Reservation only, May-September; closed to vehicles the rest of the year. Parking is very limited and there is no unreserved day use. Seasonal drawdowns affect the lake. --Claude

name: Kokosing Lake Campground (Fredericktown)

season.note: Second Friday of April through fourth Saturday of October; opening April 9, 2027.

note: Campground run by the Fredericktown Recreation District on Kokosing Lake, the Corps of Engineers flood-control lake 1.5 miles northwest of Fredericktown, at 18352 Waterford Road. Several sites along the shore; playground, large picnic area and a two-lane boat ramp. Reviewers (2019-21) fit 25-ft Class Cs and trailers; some sites have low branches. One 2020 review mentions a few long-term campers. --Claude

name: Cold Springs Campground (Yampa, Flat Tops)

season.note: Weather dependent, typically June-October.

note: Small, popular Forest Service loop 16.5 miles from Yampa on FR 900 (7 miles of paved CR 7, then gravel), with Flat Tops Wilderness views, beside a small pond and past Yamcolo Reservoir (boat launch) and Bear Lake: site 1 is a pull-through and a 24-ft camper fits site 5, but the other three are small and a ranger calls 24 ft tight. Close to the Stillwater and Smith Lake trailheads. --Claude

name: Big Kandiyohi Lake County Park East
note: Kandiyohi County park on the east shore of Big Kandiyohi Lake, 18 miles south of Willmar on County Road 8 (the west unit is a separate park). About 80 electric sites, flush toilets, hot showers, camp store, sandy beach, boat ramp, two camper cabins. May-September; daily and seasonal rates. --Claude  AWH 2026-10-11: the county's ResNexus page showed no availability on any night tried, so no rate could be read; the county opens registration each season, so re-check once 2027 registration opens. --Claude

name: Lake Snowden Campground (Hocking College)

season.note: 'Camping season runs Memorial Day through Labor Day. Subject to change.' Seasonal units out by Nov 1.

note: Public park owned by Hocking College on Lake Snowden, off US 50 at Albany, west of Athens. Beach, horse trails. Daily through seasonal stays. --Claude

name: Sheridan Bay Park Campground

season.note: Open Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day.

season_source: http://www.sheridanny.org/sheridan-bay-park.html ('The Park is open from Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day.'), read 2026-10-21
note: Town of Sheridan park on the Lake Erie shore east of Dunkirk, off NY-5. Small campground; sites with electric, small-boat access to the lake. Swimming is prohibited at the beach (no lifeguards). --Claude

name: Vastwood Park Campground
note: Hancock County park near Hawesville on the Ohio River: 400 acres with a 19-acre fishing lake, trails, disc golf and ballfields. 21 water/electric sites (30/50 amp), bathhouse with showers, dump station. Camping April through October. --Claude

name: Mill Creek Park Campground
note: Clark County Park District campground on 800-acre Mill Creek Lake near Marshall, a few miles off I-70. 139 electric sites (water from shared spigots, one per 3-4 sites), showers, dump station; boat ramp, beach, trails. name: Citizens Lake Campground
note: City of Monmouth campground on Citizens Lake at the edge of town, beside US-67 (some road noise). 30 full-hookup 30/50-amp sites, showers, dump station, playground, fishing. Open April-October. --Claude

name: Veterans Memorial Park (Jack Lake) Campground
note: Langlade County park on Jack and Game Lakes northeast of Antigo, with the Ice Age Trail through the campground. 48 electric (20/30 amp) sites, showers, dump station, cabins. Reservable; early May to mid-October. --Claude

name: Log Lake Campground
note: Kalkaska County park on small Log Lake east of Kalkaska: sandy swim beach (no lifeguard), pavilions, a disc golf course next door, the North Country Trail a mile north and the Shore-to-Shore horse trail two miles away. Caretakers on site. The county says it opens the last weekend in April. --Claude

name: Riverside Park (Mitchell County)

The sites at the north end by the boat ramp look across the ramp area to the river; the rest are screened by bank trees or set back. mycountyparks lists 'Pets prohibited' among the park's features while the camping contract gives leash rules, so ask before bringing a pet. --Claude

name: Interstate Park (Mitchell County)

season.note: Open seasonally, early May to mid-October.

season_source: https://www.mycountyparks.com/County/mitchell/Park/Interstate-Park ('Open Seasonally from early May to mid October.'), read 2026-11-03
note: Mitchell County Conservation Board park on the west edge of Mitchell, on the Cedar River pool above the Mitchell mill dam and its historic, still-operating hydro-electric powerhouse (National Register). Non-designated sites spread over the shaded interior of the park, inside the shoreline park road. Swim beach with dock, boat and canoe ramps (water trail access 263), two shelters, playgrounds; Cedar River Greenbelt trailhead nearby. --Claude

name: Otranto Park (Mitchell County)

season.note: Open seasonally early May to mid October.

season_source: https://www.mycountyparks.com/County/mitchell/Park/Otranto-Park ('Open seasonally early May to mid October.'), read 2026-11-04
note: Small Mitchell County Conservation park on the Cedar River at Otranto, a popular canoe put-in. --Claude

name: Pioneer Park (Mitchell County)

season.note: Open for camping from early May to mid October.

season_source: https://www.mycountyparks.com/County/mitchell/Park/Pioneer-Park ('Open for camping from early May to mid October.'), read 2026-11-04
note: Former state park returned to Mitchell County, 6 mi east of Osage and 4 mi north on Shadow Ave. Gravel sites; enclosed stone shelter house with electric; playground. The Little Cedar River is about 100-130 m south of the loop across a meadow, not at the sites. --Claude

name: Lake Hendricks Park

season.note: Open to camping May to October; the county turns off water and closes restrooms in early October.

season_source: https://howardcounty.iowa.gov/community/conservation-new/lake-hendricks-park/ ('open to camping from May to October') + https://howardcounty.iowa.gov/conservation/camping-page/ ('will turn off water and close restrooms in parks and campgrounds in early October'), read 2026-11-04
note: Howard County Conservation park on 54-acre Lake Hendricks north of Riceville, the county's largest and most popular park. The lower campground fills a lawn peninsula on the lake's west side; the upper campground is in woods west of the creek. A ranger lives on site year-round. --Claude

name: Cedar Bridge Park

season.note: The park page says camping is seasonal 'Early May - mid October'; the site pages say 'Open Mid May thru Mid October' and point to the county's Facebook page for opening and closing dates.

season_source: https://www.mycountyparks.com/County/Mitchell/Park/Cedar-Bridge-Park ('Camping - Seasonal: Early May - mid October') + .../Campsite-19/Availability ('Open Mid May thru Mid October - Watch our Facebook Page for Campground opening and closings'; 'Closed during Winter'), read 2026-11-03
note: Mitchell County Conservation park just west of Osage on Hwy 9, at the Cedar River Greenbelt Trail and the Milton R. Owen Nature Center. One gravel loop on open mowed ground with a playground and shelter; the Cedar River runs past the east side behind a belt of woods, with access for fishing and paddling. --Claude

name: Sandy Hollow Recreation Area

season.note: Campground open mid-April through mid-October; the park itself is open year round, 7 am to 10:30 pm.

season_source: https://www.mycountyparks.com/County/Sioux/Park/Sandy-Hollow-Recreation-Area/Facility/Sandy-Hollow-Campground/Availability ('Campground is open mid April through mid October.'; 'Campground is closed mid October to mid April.'), read 2026-11-04
note: Sioux County Conservation recreation area a mile east of Sioux Center on B40, opened 2014 around two small lakes with a swimming beach, boat ramp, kayak rental, archery range and prairie trails. The campground lines a diagonal road southwest of the west lake, behind a gravel road and a belt of shoreline trees. --Claude

name: Richey Access

season.note: Open mid-April through mid-October, weather permitting; the county announces openings and closings by email.

season_source: https://www.mycountyparks.com/County/Carroll/Park/Richey-Access/Activity/Camping ('Richey Access campground is open mid-April through mid-October, weather permitting.'), read 2026-11-04
note: Small Carroll County Conservation access 3 miles north of Ralston on the Middle Raccoon River, with canoe and kayak access. The sites line a short grass loop in the trees just west of the Apple Avenue bridge; the river runs behind a wooded bank to the north and west. --Claude

name: Alton Roadside Park

season.note: Campground open seasonally from mid-April to mid-October.

season_source: https://www.mycountyparks.com/County/Sioux/Park/Alton-Roadside-Park/Activity/Camping ('Campground open seasonally from mid April to Mid October.'), read 2026-11-03
note: Sioux County Conservation's first park (1961): 11 acres north of Alton at old Hwy 60 and Hwy 10, with a fishing pond, open and enclosed shelters, a playground, a disc golf course and seasonal modern restrooms. Park hours 7 am - 10:30 pm. Site size not posted: four electric sites, layout unconfirmed (2026-11-03). --Claude

name: Williamson Campground (Lostine River)
note: The largest of the small Wallowa-Whitman NF forest camps along the Wild and Scenic Lostine River, 11 miles up the Lostine River Road (FR 8210, paved then washboard gravel) from Lostine. 8 tent/trailer sites above the road-side bench plus 5 tent-only sites down by the river; reviewers have fit 23- and 31-ft travel trailers. Two vault toilets, no drinking water, no hookups. $10, first-come, first-served, season June-October. No cell service. --Claude

name: Walla Walla Forest Camp (Lostine River)
note: Small Wallowa-Whitman NF forest camp on the Wild and Scenic Lostine River, the first camp above the Lostine Guard Station, about 13 miles up the Lostine River Road (FR 8210) - gravel in good shape to the guard station, rockier beyond. 4 sites with tables and fire rings; sites 1 and 2 are large, and a reviewer fit a 23-ft travel trailer. Vault toilet, no drinking water, no hookups. First-come, first-served, season June-October. No cell service. --Claude

name: Turkey Flat Forest Camp (Lostine River)
note: Tiny Wallowa-Whitman NF forest camp on the Wild and Scenic Lostine River, 16 miles up the Lostine River Road (FR 8210) - rough gravel past the Lostine Guard Station. 3 sites with tables and fire rings; a reviewer fit a 23-ft travel trailer in large site 3, which has wooden steps down to the river. Vault toilet at the entrance, no drinking water, no hookups. First-come, first-served, season June-September. Eagle Cap Wilderness access; no cell service. --Claude

name: Lost Creek Campground (WY-70, Encampment)
note: Medicine Bow NF campground on the Battle Highway (WY-70) 18 miles west of Encampment, ~8,800 ft. 13 back-in sites in the trees; the FS calls them small and for trailers under 22 ft, though the measured driveways run 25-99 ft - EKKO is at the stated edge. Vault toilet, no drinking water, no trash service, no hookups. $20; some sites reservable, season mid-June to September. Baby Lakes Trail into the Huston Park Wilderness across the highway. --Claude

name: Red Mountain Campground (Cle Elum River)
note: Small Okanogan-Wenatchee NF campground between Salmon La Sac Road and the Cle Elum River north of Roslyn, ~2,300 ft. 10 single sites for tents and RVs up to 30 ft; no hookups. First-come, first-served, late May to early October. --Claude

name: East Lake Campsites (Hiawatha NF)

season_source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/hiawatha/recreation/east-lake-campsites ('Seasons of Use May 15 - Columbus Day'; 'Reservations through Columbus Day. No services/no reservations/no fees after that time Columbus Day through May 15.'), read 2026-10-25
note: Three primitive Forest Service campsites on 53-acre East Lake, Hiawatha NF (Rapid River/Manistique district), off M-94 about 22 miles north of Manistique; supplies at Steuben, two miles northwest. Unimproved, shallow, sandy back-in boat access just past site 1 (carry-in recommended). Largemouth bass, perch, bluegill and bullheads, swimming and berry picking. Pack in, pack out. --Claude

name: Lewis Wetzel WMA Campground

note: WV DNR campground in the 14,000-acre Lewis Wetzel Wildlife Management Area south of New Martinsville, near Jacksonburg (Wetzel County). First come first served. Trailheads for loop hikes leave from the campground. --Claude

name: Winston Creek Campground (DNR)
note: Forested streamside WA DNR campground in the Winston Creek forest block south of Mossyrock and Mayfield Lake, popular in elk season. 10-11 sites, vault toilets, camp host; no water or hookups. DNR says sites take trailers up to 25 ft. Closed mid-December to mid-May. First come, first served; a Discover Pass is required. --Claude

name: Middle Waddell Campground (DNR, Capitol Forest)
note: WA DNR campground in Capitol State Forest southwest of Olympia, the main hub for its ~90 miles of motorized trails - expect ORVs. About 24-33 gravel sites in three loops, mostly narrow pull-throughs good for trailers to about 27 ft, vault toilets, camp host; no water or hookups. Season May 1 to late November; 7-day limit. First come, first served; a Discover Pass is required. CLOSED for summer 2026 for hazard-tree removal (checked 2026-09-29). --Claude

name: Stuart Mill Bay Fishing Access Site

season.note: Opens the Thursday before Memorial Day; closed during the winter months

note: Montana FWP fishing access site (356 acres, ~6,400 ft) on Georgetown Lake with designated primitive camping (Region 2). Directions (FWP): 13 miles west of Anaconda on Hwy 1, turn onto Georgetown Lake Road and travel southwest about 1.5 miles to FAS sign. --Claude

name: Nahma Lakeside Landing (formerly No-Nah-Ma Resort)
note: Campground and cabins at 13723 Main St in the old sawmill town of Nahma, built on the mill slips that open onto Big Bay de Noc (Lake Michigan) beside the mouth of the Sturgeon River; most sites are on the water, with a boat ramp and rentals. Open May to October. Founded in 1997 as No-Nah-Ma Resort and sold in 2025 (Iron Mountain Daily News); it has no website of its own and books through the Campspot marketplace as Nahma Lakeside Landing Campground and Lodging LLC. Not listed on RV Life; Campspot reviewers give it 4.7 (42 reviews, 2026), one reporting low voltage (86-99 V) daily in September 2026. --Claude

name: Yogi Bear's Jellystone Park Camp-Resort Grayling

season.note: The park says 'Opening April, Closing October' (no days given).

season_source: https://www.graylingjellystone.com/contact-5 ('Season Dates: Opening April, Closing October'), read 2026-10-25
note: Franchise Jellystone Park in the woods outside Grayling.  A site may share its water and electric pedestal with another, so extension cords and extra hoses may be needed, and sewer sites are limited.  There is a pool (no lifeguard), a jumping pillow, mini golf, a Silent Disco (new in 2026) and a Bear Factory; day passes cost $15 a person, Sunday to Thursday, and early check-in $35.  The person booking must be 21 and a site holds one immediate family; e-bikes, EV charging and outside firewood aren't allowed, nor are golf carts for overnight guests.  Two dogs at most; quiet hours run from 11 p.m. to 8 a.m.  Cabins and RVs are rented. --Claude

name: Spirit Springs Campground

note: Campground in rolling hills near Marcellus, with fishing, hiking and walking trails, a pool and a playground.  RV sites have full hookups on gravel, or water, electric and greywater, with the black tank dumped at the end of the stay; power is a 110-volt plug on a 30-amp breaker, so adapters may be needed.  The Olive Branch camper and the Mustard Seed cabin are rented, there is a primitive tent site, and an extra vehicle costs $5 a day. --Claude

name: Sunset Bay RV Resort & Campground

note: RV park at River Expeditions, a rafting outfitter's adventure resort near Oak Hill by the New River Gorge (zipline, pool, hot tub, saloon); tent camping and cabins too. Pet friendly. Google 4.7 over 513 reviews (the resort as a whole). --Claude

name: Fire Pit Campground

season_source: https://firepitcampground.com/about ('The campground operates Mid-April to Mid-October'), read 2026-10-20

name: Lake Cody Campground

note: Campground on a small private lake near Elida, west of Lima. --Claude

name: Great Meadow Campground
note: Campground on Dover Rd (US-4) in Chichester east of Concord, wooded sites; nightly, weekly, monthly and seasonal stays, open May 1 to Columbus Day. Google 4.1 over 76 reviews; RV Life 4 stars. --Claude

note: Colorado Parks and Wildlife campground on CO-14 near Gould, the former Walden KOA, now a loop of State Forest State Park on open sagebrush slopes. --Claude

name: Spotted Bear Campground (Flathead NF)

A footbridge by the Spotted Bear Ranger Station (1/4 mi) reaches a sandy beach on the South Fork. High use but often has open sites midweek; a base for huckleberry picking and fishing. --Claude

name: Indian Lake Campground
note: Confederated Tribes of the Umatilla Indian Reservation campground on Indian Lake, south of Pilot Rock up a gravel road: 43 sites with fire pits and a central RV dump, no hookups, no power. $15/night (2026); reservations by phone from May 1, two-night minimum on weekends; summer season. Cash or check at the lake. --Claude

name: Annett's Mono Village
note: Resort at the west end of Upper Twin Lake, 13425 Twin Lakes Rd, Bridgeport: 250+ first-come sites (no reservations), hookup sites $45/day for 2, dry sites $35; marina and store. Seasonal (summer). RV Life 4*/$$. --Claude

name: Cumberland Cove Seaside Campground
note: Small (25-site) campground on the bank of the Northumberland Strait (227 Cumberland Cove Rd, Borden-Carleton), 10 minutes from the Confederation Bridge. Serviced sites $46, unserviced $40.25 CAD a night, taxes included. Open late June to Labour Day. Online booking (RMS). --Claude

name: Paradise Farm RV Park
note: Small seasonal RV park on Route 230 (Discovery Trail) near Bonavista, in an open loop beside a pond; 30- and 50-amp sites with water, dump station, washrooms with hot showers. Campers report ~C$40 a night (2025). A September 2025 camper was told the campground would be closing - confirm it is open before going (noted 2026-10-07). --Claude  CAMPER-REPORTED RATE: C$40 a night in September 2025 (Campendium review); the park has no web page (2026-10-11). --Claude  A September 2025 reviewer was told by phone that the campground would be closing, though they could still pull in; check before going (2026-10-11). --Claude

name: Kona Beach Park
note: Family campground on a sandy lake beach beside the Trans-Canada at South Brook, ~96 sites with electric and water, many along the beach. Showers, laundry, store, playground, dump station, paddle boat/kayak rentals. Open late May-September. Campers report C$33-35 a night (2024). --Claude  CAMPER-REPORTED RATE: C$33-40 a night in July-September 2026 (RV Life reviews); the park has no web page, only Facebook (2026-10-11). --Claude

name: The OldMill RV Park
note: Off-grid campground on the Main Brook salmon river at Avondale (72 Millville Rd): unserviced RV sites (C$22-25 a night) and a tenting field ($20), 137 sites with overflow areas. Day-use area with a small beach and swimming holes, playground; the old railbed trail starts at the gate. Open May-mid October. --Claude

name: Brookdale Country Inn & RV Park
note: Family RV park beside a country inn at Bishop's Falls (10 Main St), just off the Trans-Canada; ~43 full-service sites (30/50 amp) plus semi-serviced and tent sites, C$35-45 a night. Heated in-ground pool, fire pits. Season about mid-May to mid-October. --Claude

name: Mohawk Camping
note: Campground on Grand Lake at Waterborough, open mid-May to mid-October, with nightly and seasonal sites and boat parking. RV Life $$. --Claude  SEASONAL SHARE: 75 of its roughly 85 sites are seasonal, leaving about 10 for nightly stays, so book ahead (operator rates page; site total from RVezy; 2026-10-11). --Claude

name: Cranberry Campground
note: Family campground on a point in Merigomish Harbour (135 Weir Rd), Victoria Day to Thanksgiving; 2026 rates C$45.43 (20-amp) to $53.76 (50-amp full service) plus HST; cottages. Online booking (Newbook). --Claude  MINIMUM STAY: 2 nights from the Canada Day long weekend through the Labour Day long weekend, 3 on most long weekends (cranberrycampground.ca, 2026-10-11). --Claude

name: River Ryan Campground
note: Campground on the Union Hwy at River Ryan near New Waterford, Cape Breton, open May-October, ~42 sites. RV Life 5*, $$. --Claude

name: Forest Hills Cabins & RV Park
note: Cabins and pull-through RV sites near Carberry, open May to Thanksgiving; RV sites C$35 + GST a night, $185 a week, seasonal sites too. Online booking. --Claude

name: Edson Lions Park Campground
note: Town campground in Edson on Highway 16, open May to September; 27 sites with power and 16 without; register at the park office. --Claude

name: Camping Baie du Diable
note: Large campground (316 sites, a big seasonal share) on the point between the Baskatong reservoir and its Baie du Diable arm near Ferme-Neuve, with a long sand beach and a marina; full-hookup Pionniers section on the point, 30A Aventuriers section to the north-east. Posted rates C$50 water+electric / C$60 full hookup + tax (2024 table, still the operator's list in 2026; the official 2026 maximum is the same C$60). Reservations by phone only, 30% non-refundable deposit. Season mid-May to early October. --Claude

name: Camping la Descente des Femmes
note: 46-site village campground at Sainte-Rose-du-Nord on the Saguenay fjord (26 three-service 15A RV sites, 20 tent sites), with an artificial swimming pond. 3-service sites C$45 a night for up to 4 people (operator reservation page; the official 2026 maximum is C$45). RV sites by phone reservation, tents first-come; cash only. Season June to mid-October; the operator site was last updated in 2024. --Claude

name: Camping Causapscal chez Moose
note: 84-site campground on five terraces at Causapscal in the Matapédia valley (Route 132), with 3-service sites 70-85 ft long; July is rented by the day only. Official 2026 maximum C$52 a night (2025 operator table C$40-48, taxes included; 2027 not yet posted). Booked online. Season early June to early September. --Claude

name: Camping du Rivage
note: 38-site seaside campground on the St. Lawrence beach at Sainte-Anne-des-Monts (Gaspésie), 2 km from downtown and 20 min from Parc national de la Gaspésie; 15/30A water+electric or full-hookup sites, dump station. RV 2-service C$55 / 3-service C$60 a night, taxes included (C$47.84 / C$52.19 before tax; the official 2026 maximum is C$52.19). Booking by phone or e-mail. Season mid-May to mid-October. --Claude

name: Camping Domaine Ensoleillé 2000
note: 65-unit seaside campground on Route 138 at Baie-Trinité (Îlets-Caribou, Côte-Nord, Whale Route), above a tidal bay of the St. Lawrence with a sandy beach; unserviced seaside sites, 1-service panoramic sites and 3-service 20/30A sites (some for 40 ft+); restaurant, store. Official 2026 maximum C$54.95 a night for any campsite; booked online. Season mid-May to late September. --Claude

name: Camping Sainte-Madeleine
note: 282-site campground beside Autoroute 20 exit 120 at Sainte-Madeleine (traffic noise on the east side), about 200 sites seasonal and 77 sold online; the Rivière Huron runs through the park; pool, splash pad, disc golf. 2026: one night C$55 water+electric, C$59 3-service + tax (10% off before 4 June and after 14 September); a July 2027 weeknight sells online at C$59. Season about May to September. --Claude

name: Aintree Trailer Park
note: Family campground in Kincardine a short walk from the Lake Huron beach: 150 seasonal sites (1-5 year waitlist) and about 21 overnight sites - two-point back-in (30A, water, up to 40 ft), full-service back-in and drive-through, small-trailer/tent sites. 2026 rates including tax: two-point back-in C$71 (C$62.83 before HST), full service C$75 a night; one night to a few months. Booked online, one-day deposit per week. Season 7 May-Thanksgiving Monday. --Claude

name: Bella Coola Valley Campground & Cabins
note: Family-run campground (est. 2021) at 1875 Highway 20, Hagensborg, beside the Augsburg Church in the Bella Coola Valley: full-hookup 20A sites 1-9 for small and mid-size units, 30A full-hookup sites 15-16 for rigs over 30 ft, power-only 20A sites, tent sites along two small creeks, and three spruce cabins; shower house with flush toilets, coin showers and laundry, sani-station. Posted nightly prices including tax: full hookup C$42.00 per unit, power-only C$36.75, unserviced C$31.50. Reservations by e-mail, text or phone (site numbers first-come; no long-term stays). Season May-October. Caveat: the Hwy 20 'Hill' into the valley has steep gravel grades. --Claude

name: Prairie Ridge A Loop (Rathbun Lake)

season.note: Campground season May - September; closed October - April (USACE). Rates run May 15 - September 14.

season_source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/233593 (facility_phone: 'FOR CAMPGROUND INQUIRIES DURING MAY-SEPTEMBER PLEASE CALL 641-724-3103. DURING CLOSED SEASON OCTOBER-APRIL PLEASE CALL 641-647-2464') + rates (Peak Season 2026-05-15 to 2026-09-14), read 2026-11-03
note: USACE Rathbun Lake campground on a high prairie ridge between Buck Creek and Honey Creek, SW of Moravia; the last 2.5 miles in are gravel (200th Avenue). Woodland draws and timbered hillsides, a modern playground, and a boat ramp sheltered on three sides with a courtesy dock and fish-cleaning station. An 8-mile trail links to Honey Creek Resort. Unstaffed. --Claude
